narr: An upper-level low off the coast of California helped funnel in subtropical moisture into the state resulting in the development of widespread showers and storms across central and eastern New Mexico June 5th and 6th. Reports of severe weather and flash flooding stretched from the Rio Grande Valley across portions of eastern NM on June 5th. These reports ranged from a landspout tornado near the Petroglyph National Monument and Nara Visa, NM to flash flooding. Another round of severe weather began in the afternoon of June 6th producing more widespread reports over the same area of the state. Reports ranged from burn scar flash flooding within the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and Santa Rosa, to large hail over parts of San Miguel County.
ev: Flash flooding reported across Santa Rosa via NM State EOC and County EM. Extent of impacts and potential damages are unknown.

At least one foot of hail accumulation was reported in flooded areas. Via Sedillo was washed over with large rocks, mud, and debris in several spots. Culverts and ditches completely overflowed. Water marks indicated at least 6 inches of water flowed over Via Sedillo in some spots.

Local Volunteer Fire Dept. relayed reports of burn scar flash flooding. Debris and water over roadways in and around Cabo Lucero stretching down to San Geronimo an hour later. No damage to structures. Timing estimated and based on radar.
Vehicle stuck in flood waters and partially submerged in mud along Sedillo Road.
NMDOT reported severe driving conditions from standing water and flooding over roadways in the Estancia area.
Several inches of hail and water was reported flowing from a nearby pasture across a dirt road in northern San Miguel County.
